welcome.title: Welcome — start here
welcome.transcript:
Welcome to White Tee Research, our shared library for building a plain white T-shirt brand.

We are starting with the competitive landscape. Our first three profiles cover ASKET, Son of a Tailor, and True Classic. Each explores the product, price, brand message, customer evidence, and what we might learn. Their current ranges extend beyond a single product, and these first profiles are a starting point, not a complete market survey.

You can listen to audio briefs directly on this site. Use the play and pause controls, drag the progress bar to skip ahead, or download the MP3. The transcript stays tucked away until you select Show transcript. Audio is generated locally on our Mac from written text, without a paid speech service.

Later, the research will inform our customer persona, brand direction, and website plan. Archetype branding, persuasion principles, and modern or postmodern design are possibilities to explore, not decisions we have already made.

To improve any page, use Suggest a change. It opens a GitHub issue with the page link included. A GitHub account is required, and submitted feedback is public.

asket.title: Listen to the 60-second ASKET brief
asket.transcript:
ASKET shows how a plain white T-shirt can compete on detail.

In our November ninth research, its white tee cost sixty-five dollars. It uses organic long-staple cotton, with three length options and production in Portugal. ASKET now sells a broader essentials collection, so it is a product benchmark for us, rather than a single-product business.

Its likely appeal is to shoppers who want understated clothing and specific information about fit and materials. We interpret its brand personality as the Sage, with Creator cues: explain the product, then keep refining it.

Through Cialdini's lens, production knowledge offers authority cues, while customer reviews provide social proof. These are interpretations of its messaging, not proof that it increases sales.

Our takeaway: make quality visible through fabric details, fit guidance, and clear photographs. Before adopting premium pricing ourselves, test the shirt's opacity, wash performance, and whether customers value different lengths.

son-of-a-tailor.title: Listen to the Son of a Tailor brief
son-of-a-tailor.transcript:
Son of a Tailor

Angle: custom fit and made-to-order production · Market: USD storefront · Reviewed: November 9, 2026

The offer

The brand calls its cotton T-shirt its first product. Today the range also includes polos, shirts, and knitwear: a T-shirt-led specialist that has expanded, not a single-product business. Product · Current assortment.

Product. Observed details: Cotton T-Shirt, Medium Weight, White

Single-shirt price. Observed details: US$75; bundle promotion shown separately

Fabric. Observed details: 100% Supima cotton; 150 grams per square meter jersey

Fit & production. Observed details: Custom and standard sizes; made to order in Portugal

Timing & shipping. Observed details: 7–10 days production; free shipping on two or more items

Fit assurance. Observed details: Free remake if dissatisfied with the fit of the first order

Source: product page, including Shipping and Guarantee tabs. Production time is not delivery time. Single-item shipping, taxes, and refund conditions were not verified. A remake guarantee should not be treated as a refund policy.

The brand

Fit is the central promise, supported by material and production explanations. The page explicitly notes slight translucency in the white tee. Interpretation: customization and fit assurance reduce purchase uncertainty; production detail supports credibility. These are observed messaging choices, not proof of conversion effectiveness.

Archetypes & persuasion

Tentative archetype: Creator, with Sage cues. Making a garment around the wearer suggests craftsmanship and individuality. The sizing explanation adds expertise. This is our interpretation of the mission and sizing process, not a declared brand identity.

Authority. Observed evidence: Named production facility and partner expertise on the production page. Interpretation and limit: Concrete production knowledge supports credibility; the brand’s claims still need independent checks.

Social proof. Observed evidence: Trustpilot reference displayed on the tee page. Interpretation and limit: A review signal, not proof about this exact white variant.

Risk reduction — outside the seven. Observed evidence: First-order fit remake offered on the tee page. Interpretation and limit: Addresses uncertainty about fit; it is not automatically reciprocity.

For our tee: test whether a simple fit guide provides enough reassurance before pursuing custom manufacturing. Personalization alone does not demonstrate commitment/consistency. Framework and comparison.

Customer evidence

The product page displayed a Trustpilot reference of 4.6/5 from 2,638 reviews. We did not independently inspect those reviews, so we cannot summarize recurring praise or complaints or assume the score concerns this SKU. Displayed review reference.

What we can learn

Takeaway: fit can be the product’s main differentiator; disclose material tradeoffs clearly. Test: willingness to wait for custom fit versus immediate shipping. Unknown: independent customer experience, full refund terms, and whether the white fabric’s translucency fits our intended use.

true-classic.title: Listen to the True Classic brief
true-classic.transcript:
True Classic

Angle: flattering fit, value, and promotional merchandising · Market: US · Reviewed: November 9, 2026

The offer

True Classic’s product page positions the tee around appearance, comfort, and value. Its navigation and cross-sells include pants, outerwear, and other categories: a broader apparel benchmark today. Product and assortment.

Product. Observed details: Classic Crew Neck, White; single; regular length; straight hem

Displayed regular price. Observed details: $34.99 USD

Observed promotion. Observed details: $29.99 USD, labeled Black Friday; membership pricing is separate

Fabric. Observed details: Cotton/polyester jersey, described as a 60/40 blend; grams per square meter not found

Fit options. Observed details: S–4XL; short, regular, or tall; straight or curved hem options

Shipping & guarantee. Observed details: Page displayed free shipping and a 100-day guarantee; detailed conditions not verified

Source: product page. No size was selected, so this does not confirm stock for every combination. Taxes and final delivery charges were not checked. The page warns of up to 5% shrinkage under normal washing and drying.

The brand

The page combines customer counts, ratings, try-on videos, sale pricing, multipacks, and membership offers. Interpretation: social proof is prominent; discount comparisons provide price anchors. The number of options could also add buying complexity. These are hypotheses about the experience, not measured outcomes.

Archetypes & persuasion

Tentative archetype: Everyperson, with aspirational confidence cues. Everyday fit problems and customer try-ons make the promise relatable. The appearance-focused language adds aspiration, but is insufficient to establish a separate Hero archetype. Evidence: tee page.

Social proof. Observed evidence: Customer counts, review totals, and try-on videos on the tee page. Interpretation and limit: Popularity and peer experience are prominent; counts are brand-displayed, not audited by us.

Liking — plausible. Observed evidence: Everyday-customer presentation and conversational fit language on the same page. Interpretation and limit: May make the messenger relatable; actual affinity needs customer testing.

Scarcity — not established. Observed evidence: Black Friday pricing appears on the same page. Interpretation and limit: A promotional label alone does not verify a real deadline or limited stock.

For our tee: test honest try-on examples with useful size context. Discounts are price framing; membership benefits alone do not prove unity. Framework and comparison.

Customer evidence

The page displayed 4.5/5 from 71,037 reviews. In the first five displayed entries, appearance and fit were recurring positives; others mentioned quality or delivery. All five were five-star entries, and two shared the same reviewer name. They are not a representative sample or confirmed white-only reviews. Complaint themes remain unresearched. Product reviews.

What we can learn

Takeaway: connect product features to an understandable wearing benefit. Test: a simple single-shirt offer versus bundles. Unknown: opacity, long-term durability, negative-review themes, and complete guarantee terms.
